questionText: In a B+ tree, the requirement of at least half-full (50%) node occupancy is relaxed for which one of the following cases?
explanation:
Step 1: Understand B+ Tree Node Occupancy Rules
In a B+ tree of order $p$ (where order represents the maximum number of children or pointers per node):
- Internal nodes (except the root) must have at least $\lceil p/2 \rceil$ children.
- Leaf nodes (except when the root is also a leaf) must be at least 50% full.

Step 2: Identify the Exception
The root node is an exception to the minimum occupancy condition. The root can have as few as 2 children (or containing as few as 1 key) when the tree is small or just growing, violating the strict 50% minimum node occupancy constraint that applies to all other nodes.

Conclusion:
Thus, the requirement of at least half-full occupancy is relaxed only for the root node.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
